standard_prerequisites.name: The two fibre classes of a cycle on a product with the projective line
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-rational-equivalence-family, invoked at proof lines 6504 and 6515
standard_prerequisites.use: Realises a rationally trivial cycle alpha as the difference of the two pullbacks of a single cycle beta on the product with the projective line, and later supplies the rational equivalence of the two pushes forward of c cap beta. That lemma is claimed separately as S14-algebra-rational-equiv-family.

core_obligations: Make sense of the statement: for a triple whose line bundle restricts to the structure sheaf on the divisor, the Gysin operation is defined on the level of cycles, so evaluating the rule on cycles is legitimate (proof lines 6495-6501).

Realise the vanishing condition: for a cycle alpha rationally equivalent to zero, use the family lemma to find a cycle beta on the product with the projective line whose two pullbacks along the standard sections differ by alpha (proof lines 6502-6508).

Conclude: the two standard sections are effective Cartier divisors with trivial normal bundles, so the assumed weak form of condition (3) applies and c cap alpha is the difference of the two pushes forward of c cap beta; those two pushes forward are rationally equivalent by the family lemma again, whence c cap alpha = 0 (proof lines 6508-6515).
proof_roadmap: Check that the rule may be evaluated on cycles (proof lines 6495-6501).
Write a rationally trivial cycle as the difference of the two fibre pullbacks of one cycle on the product with the projective line (proof lines 6502-6508).
Apply the assumed condition to the two standard sections and use the rational equivalence of the two pushes forward (proof lines 6508-6515).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a rule satisfying the bivariant condition (3) only for divisors whose conormal bundle is trivial already annihilates rationally trivial cycles, hence factors through rational equivalence (statement lines 6476-6493, tag 0FDZ). The proof is short but it is a real computation: it first has to justify evaluating the rule on cycles through the Gysin operation on cycles, then writes a rationally trivial cycle as the difference of the two fibre pullbacks of one cycle on the product with the projective line, applies the hypothesis to the two standard sections whose conormal bundles are trivial, and closes with the rational equivalence of the two resulting classes. The realisation through the product with the projective line is the substance, so the claim is H2.
